workload: 8 deterministic dev queries per task, each with all 100 saved full-corpus Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B candidates; Ecom, Cmedqa, T2
timing: wall time from prepared real text through client tokenization, HTTP classification scoring and response parsing; model/data setup excluded; ranking-inclusive times also in sweep/results.json

recommended_tested_configuration.input: explicit token IDs with task-specific instruction and HF model-card prefix/suffix

comparison.aggregation: arithmetic mean of four trials per task/client: two before and two after the other server configurations
comparison.only_changed_setting: client concurrency 1 -> 2; same server32/token16384 and request batch128

quality_checks.hf_reference: 48 real pairs, full original HF causal LM, eager FP16 on the same NPU; recomputed vLLM scores for each server configuration
quality_checks.limitation: This checks serving behavior and configuration stability, not full CMTEB-R accuracy or reproduction of the published 75.94. Eight queries per task are not a reliable estimate of task-wide accuracy.

other_findings: 128 sequences / 32768 tokens with client128/concurrency2 gave 26482, 26610, 25515 tok/s for Ecom, Cmedqa, T2: small tradeoffs rather than an overall improvement.
256 max sequences regressed short-input throughput to about 22926 tok/s at client128/concurrency2.
Client256/concurrency4 did not beat client128/concurrency2 and increased request latency.
Explicit async scheduling was enabled successfully but added no meaningful throughput improvement.
Graph compilation, quantization, prefix caching and input-length reductions were not used.
Temporary benchmark server was stopped and port18225 was verified closed after completion.
